title: US-Iran War Escalates Into Ninth Day as Tehran Strikes Gulf Bases and Warns of Full Offensive
excerpt: Iran has launched missile strikes on US military installations across Bahrain, Jordan, Kuwait and Qatar, killing at least three American soldiers, as a senior adviser warns of imminent full-scale offensive operations.
body:
• The US has struck Iranian targets for nine consecutive days, hitting military infrastructure, a nuclear facility under construction at Darkhovin, and a bridge linking Bandar Abbas to Kehuristan
  • Iran retaliated with missile and drone strikes on US bases in Bahrain, Jordan, Kuwait and Qatar, killing at least three American service members
  • Senior military adviser Mohsen Rezaei warned Iran would enter "full-scale offensive operations" if US strikes continue, while Tehran suspended its commitments to the June MOU
  • Brent crude surged above $90 per barrel as Strait of Hormuz traffic slowed to a trickle, with US gasoline prices up over 30% since the war began

Nine Days of Strikes, Three Americans Dead

The United States struck Iranian targets for the ninth consecutive day on Sunday, as the conflict that erupted on February 28 descended into what Reuters described as a "full-blown war once again." The latest strikes, ordered by President Trump at around 6 p.m. ET on Saturday, targeted Iranian military coastal surveillance and air-defense facilities, US Central Command confirmed.

Among the targets was the partly built Darkhovin nuclear power plant in southwestern Iran, according to Tehran's Atomic Energy Organization, which called it "a clear violation of international law." US forces also destroyed a bridge linking Bandar Abbas and Kehuristan, and struck sites near Sirik in Hormozgan Province and Shadegan.

https://x.com/TheMichaelEvery/status/2079005572985495973

The escalation followed the killing of two US military personnel and the disappearance of a third in an Iranian missile attack on a base in Jordan on Friday night. The deaths bring the American toll since the war began to at least 16 killed and more than 420 wounded, according to Central Command.

"Iran has been very, very badly damaged. They've lost everything almost militarily. They've got very little left."

— US President Donald Trump

Iran Retaliates Across Four Countries

Tehran responded with a broad campaign of missile and drone strikes against US military installations in Bahrain, Jordan, Kuwait and Qatar. Iranian military statements said missiles struck aircraft hangars, fuel storage areas and communications infrastructure at Bahrain's Sheikh Isa Air Base, triggering multiple air raid sirens.

Jordan's military announced its air defense systems intercepted 10 Iranian missiles. In Qatar, missile debris injured a child. Kuwait reported strikes damaging power plants, water desalination facilities and other civilian infrastructure — an escalation beyond purely military targets.

Iran's state broadcaster warned people to "stay away from US bases," adding: "If you want to remain safe from Iran's missiles, summon your courage and assert your independence, and shut down U.S. military bases on your territory."

Full-Scale Offensive Warning

Mohsen Rezaei, an adviser to Iranian Supreme Leader Mojtaba Khamenei, warned on Friday that "if US strikes continue for several more days, we will move into a phase of full-scale offensive operations." The statement marks a shift from Tehran's previous framing of its actions as purely defensive retaliation.

Iran's Deputy Foreign Minister Kazem Gharibabadi confirmed Saturday that Tehran had "suspended our commitments" to the memorandum of understanding with the United States, brokered by Pakistan in June. "We are not implementing them, and we are busy defending the country," he said.

The IRGC warned that the Strait of Hormuz "will not be safe" for ships carrying "a single drop of oil and gas" as long as "US aggression" persists. The Revolutionary Guards claimed two oil tankers exploded in mined waters near the strait and four commercial vessels were stopped.

Oil Surges, India Braces for Impact

Brent crude rose back above $90 per barrel on Monday, July 20, for the first time since early June. Traffic through the Strait of Hormuz — historically the route for one-fifth of global energy supplies — has slowed to a trickle. US retail gasoline prices, already up more than 30% since the war began, have climbed back above $4 per gallon.

For India, the escalation compounds an already severe energy crisis. India imports approximately 85% of its crude oil, with a significant share historically transiting the Strait of Hormuz. Rising oil prices directly inflate India's import bill, widen its current account deficit, and drive up fuel and food costs domestically.

"The Islamic Republic started this latest round of violence in the region and is now struggling to explain away its embrace of a scorched-earth policy against its neighbors."

— Behnam Ben Taleblu, Iran Program Director, Foundation for Defending Democracies

Millions of Indian workers across the Gulf face mounting security risks. Bahrain, Kuwait, Qatar and Jordan — all hosting large Indian diaspora populations — have come under direct Iranian fire. The international airport and seaport in Aqaba, Jordan were evacuated on Sunday due to "a specific and credible threat," the US embassy confirmed. With F-16s deploying from Germany and F-35s from Britain, military analysts warn the conflict shows no signs of de-escalation.
image_caption: Satellite image of the Strait of Hormuz between Iran and the Arabian Peninsula. The IRGC has warned the strategic waterway will not be safe for oil tankers as the US-Iran conflict enters its ninth consecutive day of strikes.
nri_angle: Iranian strikes on US bases in Bahrain, Kuwait, Qatar and Jordan threaten millions of Indian workers in the Gulf, while surging oil prices hit India's economy.
